paragraphs: A system that combines several sensing modalities faces two changing conditions: how much computation it can use and how trustworthy each input is. A fixed network cannot readily adjust to a smaller compute budget. It can also waste computation on a badly corrupted input when another modality offers more useful information.

ADMN addresses both issues by changing the number of active layers. It adjusts the total depth used across modalities to satisfy resource constraints, then redistributes those layers according to input quality. This makes allocation sensitive to both the available resources and the information those resources will process. The adaptation happens at the level of layers rather than treating every modality as a fixed computational commitment.

The evaluations show that ADMN can match the accuracy of state-of-the-art networks while using up to 75% fewer floating-point operations. That is a reported maximum reduction, rather than a saving promised in every setting. The result supports jointly adapting computational depth and modality allocation when resource availability and sensor quality fluctuate.
neurips-2025-admn-a-layer-wise-adaptive-.tldr: ADMN adapts network depth to compute budgets and input quality, matching leading accuracy with up to 75% fewer floating-point operations.

paragraphs: Reinforcement learning policies can struggle when an environment behaves differently from the model used during training. This paper addresses that uncertainty by training policies on unfavorable trajectories generated with a diffusion model. The aim is to improve behavior under difficult dynamics, rather than relying only on trajectories that reflect typical outcomes.

Diffusion models provide two useful capabilities here. They can generate complete trajectories together, mitigating the accumulating errors associated with predicting each transition separately. They can also condition generation toward particular distributions. AD-RRL uses that conditional generation to guide the diffusion process toward worst-case trajectories during policy training.

The training objective connects to Conditional Value at Risk, or CVaR, which focuses on the unfavorable part of the return distribution. Through an established connection between CVaR optimization and robust reinforcement learning, the generated trajectories support policies that account for dynamics uncertainty. Across standard benchmarks, the authors report better robustness and performance than existing robust reinforcement learning methods. These findings support adversarial trajectory generation as an effective empirical approach to robust policy training.
neurips-2025-adversarial-diffusion-for-r.tldr: AD-RRL guides diffusion models toward worst-case training trajectories to improve reinforcement learning robustness under uncertain environment dynamics.

paragraphs: Mobile agents often send the entire phone interface to a cloud language model at each step. That gives the model useful context but also exposes information unrelated to the task. Running everything locally avoids these uploads, yet smaller local models have lower task success rates. CORE divides the work between local and cloud models.

First, it groups related interface elements into blocks using the screen's XML hierarchy. Local and cloud models then collaborate to identify the current subtask. The local model ranks relevant blocks, and the cloud model chooses a specific element within the highest-ranked block. A mechanism that accumulates information across rounds helps address local ranking errors or insufficient context.

Across the evaluated applications and tasks, CORE reduces interface exposure by up to 55.6%. Task success remains slightly below that of cloud-only agents. The result therefore demonstrates a concrete tradeoff: substantially less interface information reaches the cloud while task performance stays close to the cloud-only approach. It does not imply that all uploads or privacy exposure disappear.
neurips-2025-core-reducing-ui-exposure-i.tldr: CORE coordinates local and cloud models to reduce mobile interface exposure by up to 55.6%, with task success slightly below cloud-only agents.

paragraphs: Deploying proprietary language models on edge devices brings their capabilities closer to users, supporting efficiency and privacy. It also creates opportunities for attackers to extract model weights and architecture, enabling unauthorized copies. The paper further considers exploitation through techniques such as fine-tuning, even when a defense prevents complete extraction of the weights.

CoreGuard targets the cost of protecting these deployments. Existing defenses can require substantial computation and communication, undermining their practicality on edge devices. The proposed method combines a protection protocol designed to reduce computational overhead with a propagation protocol designed to minimize communication overhead. Both costs are part of the protection problem because an expensive defense can weaken the motivation for deploying locally.

The authors report extensive experiments in which CoreGuard achieves what they describe as upper-bound security protection with negligible overhead. This is the stated experimental finding, rather than an unrestricted promise against every attack. The contribution is a protection approach intended to preserve foundational model capabilities while keeping the computational and communication burden small enough for edge deployment.
neurips-2025-coreguard-safeguarding-foun.tldr: CoreGuard protects edge-deployed language models against stealing and exploitation while reporting negligible computational and communication overhead.

paragraphs: Tracing an unauthorized derivative language model is difficult when investigators cannot inspect its parameters or when fine-tuning weakens existing identification methods. ErrorTrace approaches this problem through patterns of mistakes. Its central idea is that model families have distinctive error patterns that can provide evidence of lineage despite changes to individual models.

The method maps and analyzes these family-specific error spaces. It operates as a black-box mechanism, without requiring internal parameters or relying on specific query responses. The identifying signal is the structure of errors associated with a family. This makes the proposed approach relevant to tracing derivatives whose internal implementation is inaccessible.

For 27 base models, ErrorTrace reports traceability accuracy of 0.8518 when the suspect model is excluded from its training set, exceeding the baseline by 0.2593. It also successfully tracks 34 models modified through fine-tuning, pruning, or merging across the tested scenarios. These results support robustness to several forms of model modification. The authors additionally report some resilience to adversarial attacks, a qualified finding that does not establish immunity to them.
neurips-2025-errortrace-a-black-box-trac.tldr: ErrorTrace identifies model lineage through family-specific error patterns, enabling black-box tracing across several tested forms of model modification.

paragraphs: A prediction model can change the population it serves. Users receiving accurate predictions may engage more, invite others, or adopt behaviors that bring similar users into the system. Subsequent learning then takes place on a changed population. Evolutionary prediction games formalize this feedback between prediction quality, user behavior, and repeated model training.

The framework draws on evolutionary game theory, treating the growth and decline of user groups as a natural-selection process. In idealized settings with unlimited data and computation, the theoretical analysis finds that repeated learning promotes competition and competitive exclusion across a broad class of behavioral dynamics. Better-served groups can therefore gain an advantage through the learning feedback itself.

The picture changes under constraints such as finite data, limited computation, or overfitting risk. The authors show that stable coexistence and mutually beneficial relationships between groups become possible. They analyze when these arrangements are feasible and stable, describe mechanisms that can sustain them, and demonstrate their findings empirically. The distinction matters: realistic constraints permit coexistence, but the result does not say they inevitably produce it.
neurips-2025-evolutionary-prediction-gam.tldr: Evolutionary prediction games show how learning–population feedback can promote exclusion under idealized conditions while permitting coexistence under realistic constraints.

paragraphs: AutoGraph generates attributed graphs by turning them into token sequences that a decoder-only transformer can model autoregressively. The conversion uses random sequences and is reversible, so the sequence representation retains the graph information needed to reconstruct it. This connects graph generation to the sequence-generation approach used in language modeling.

A central design property is that sequence prefixes represent induced subgraphs. Partial sequences therefore correspond to meaningful partial graph structures. The method also avoids additional node features that are expensive to compute. Its sequence lengths and sampling complexity grow linearly with the number of edges, making the representation particularly suitable for large, sparse graphs.

On synthetic and molecular benchmarks, the authors report state-of-the-art performance, with generation up to 100 times faster and training up to three times faster than leading diffusion models. AutoGraph also supports generation conditioned on a substructure without fine-tuning. Its reported transferability is promising, rather than an established general-purpose graph foundation capability. Together, the results show how an appropriate reversible representation can make standard transformer machinery effective for graph generation.
neurips-2025-flatten-graphs-as-sequences.tldr: AutoGraph reversibly represents graphs as token sequences, enabling scalable transformer generation with strong benchmark results and substantial reported speedups.

paragraphs: Continual learning asks a language model to learn tasks sequentially while retaining earlier capabilities. LoRA supports parameter-efficient adaptation, and many continual-learning methods add a separate LoRA branch for each new task. The problem identified here is how those branches are combined: giving new and old branches equal influence on earlier tasks can contribute to forgetting.

GainLoRA keeps the practice of adding a branch for each task but introduces gates to control how the branches are integrated. In particular, the new gating module is used to minimize the new branch's influence on old tasks. The method therefore targets interference between adaptations, allowing new learning while reducing its disruption of previously learned behavior.

Experiments on continual-learning benchmarks show that GainLoRA outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods. The authors attribute the improvement to mitigating forgetting through controlled integration of old and new branches. The practical lesson is that adding task-specific adaptation capacity is only part of the problem; deciding how that capacity affects earlier tasks also matters. The reported result is reduced forgetting and improved overall performance, rather than complete elimination of forgetting.
neurips-2025-gated-integration-of-low-ra.tldr: GainLoRA uses gates to limit interference from new LoRA branches, reducing forgetting as language models learn tasks sequentially.

paragraphs: Generalized linear bandits model sequential choices whose rewards depend on context through a nonlinear link function. This accommodates reward distributions such as Bernoulli and Poisson. The challenge is to make good decisions while keeping each update inexpensive: prior methods commonly sacrifice either computational efficiency or the statistical quality of their decisions.

The paper proposes an algorithm that combines nearly optimal regret with constant time and space per round. Regret measures the performance lost through imperfect choices during learning. The estimator updates in one pass using online mirror descent, avoiding the need for costly repeated processing as observations arrive. The contribution is a guarantee that this efficient update can still support statistically strong decisions.

The key theoretical ingredient is a tight confidence set for the estimator, derived using mix loss from online prediction. That confidence set supports an optimistic decision rule that accounts for uncertainty. The analysis shows statistical efficiency comparable to maximum likelihood estimation despite one-pass updates. Thus, the result joins computational and statistical efficiency rather than treating fast updates as a reason to accept substantially weaker regret guarantees.
neurips-2025-generalized-linear-bandits-.tldr: A one-pass generalized linear bandit algorithm combines nearly optimal regret with constant per-round time and space through tighter uncertainty analysis.

paragraphs: Composed image retrieval searches using both an image and a textual modification. This paper introduces i-CIR, an evaluation dataset focused on finding the same particular object under the requested changes. Preserving object identity makes the task more specific than retrieving any image from the appropriate semantic category.

The dataset stays compact by selecting difficult negative examples through a semi-automated process. The authors describe its challenge as comparable to searching among more than 40 million random distractors; that does not mean the dataset itself contains that many images. To address the difficulty of collecting suitable training data, they also introduce BASIC, a training-free method built on pretrained vision-and-language models.

BASIC separately measures similarity to the query image and the query text, then combines the scores late in the process. Images that satisfy both parts receive more weight, while strong agreement with only one part is downweighted. Additional components improve the individual similarities. BASIC achieves new state-of-the-art results on i-CIR and existing semantic-level retrieval datasets, supporting joint satisfaction of the visual and textual requirements as a useful retrieval principle.
neurips-2025-instance-level-composed-ima.tldr: The paper introduces an object-identity retrieval benchmark and BASIC, a training-free method that combines image and text similarity to satisfy both query requirements.

paragraphs: DNA modeling requires understanding dependencies that can span more than 10,000 base pairs while considering information in both directions. The paper identifies a training tradeoff: autoregressive learning is efficient but unidirectional, whereas masked modeling supports bidirectional understanding but computes loss only for masked tokens. JanusDNA introduces a pretraining approach intended to combine the advantages of both.

Its architecture combines Mamba, attention, and mixture-of-experts layers. Attention supplies global context at high resolution, Mamba supports efficient sequence representation, and sparse expert activation increases capacity while keeping computation manageable. Together with the pretraining approach, this hybrid design addresses both long sequences and bidirectional comprehension.

The authors report processing up to one million base pairs at single-nucleotide resolution on one 80GB GPU. Experiments and ablations show new state-of-the-art performance on three genomic representation benchmarks, including surpassing models with 250 times more activated parameters. These are distinct efficiency findings: one concerns sequence capacity on specified hardware, while the other concerns parameters activated during computation. The results support the effectiveness of the combined architecture and training design on the evaluated genomic tasks.
neurips-2025-janusdna-a-powerful-bi-dire.tldr: JanusDNA combines bidirectional pretraining with Mamba, attention, and sparse experts to model long DNA sequences efficiently and improve genomic benchmark performance.

paragraphs: When predicting several outcomes from multiple kinds of data, the best processing strategy may differ between people. Text may be more informative for one sample, numeric features for another, and the benefits of sharing information between prediction tasks may also vary. This paper makes those choices adaptive rather than fixing them for the entire dataset.

The architecture offers multiple pathways, including raw and combined representations of text and numeric features. A learned router selects a modality–task expert combination for each input. Depending on that decision, predictions use shared or independent output heads. The routing and prediction components are trained together, allowing the system to learn how input processing and task sharing should interact.

Evaluations use synthetic data and psychotherapy notes to predict depression and anxiety outcomes. The method consistently outperforms the tested fixed multitask and single-task baselines. Its routing decisions also provide interpretable information about which modalities matter and how tasks relate across samples. The findings support per-subject adaptation when data quality and task relationships vary, without establishing clinical benefits beyond the reported prediction experiments.
neurips-2025-learning-to-route-per-sampl.tldr: A learned router adapts modality processing and task sharing for each sample, improving depression and anxiety prediction over tested fixed strategies.

paragraphs: Mathematical reasoning about figures requires connecting individual reasoning steps to the relevant visual information. Existing approaches can be constrained by rectangular image regions, vision encoders that poorly capture mathematical content, or dependence on external tools for visual modification. MINT-CoT introduces a mechanism for inserting relevant visual tokens directly into textual reasoning.

An Interleave Token dynamically selects regions of arbitrary shape within mathematical figures. To train this capability, the authors build a dataset of 54,000 mathematical problems with reasoning steps aligned to visual regions at the token level. Training proceeds through text-only supervised reasoning, supervised reasoning with interleaved visual tokens, and reinforcement learning with the interleaved format.

This process produces MINT-CoT-7B. The authors report improvements over the baseline of 34.08% on MathVista and 28.78% on GeoQA. These results support the effectiveness of the combined data, training, and token-interleaving approach for visual mathematical reasoning. The central contribution is a closer connection between a particular reasoning step and the figure information it uses, with visual selection that is not restricted to coarse rectangular regions.
neurips-2025-mint-cot-enabling-interleav.tldr: MINT-CoT interleaves selected visual tokens with mathematical reasoning steps, improving results on MathVista and GeoQA through aligned data and staged training.

paragraphs: Detecting generated images becomes difficult when a detector encounters generators or scenarios different from those represented during development. This paper investigates image entropy as a cue that may generalize across sources. The goal is to capture useful image statistics while reducing dependence on the semantic content depicted in an image.

The proposed Multi-granularity Local Entropy Patterns, or MLEP, are feature maps computed using Shannon entropy. They are constructed from shuffled small patches at multiple image scales. This process captures pixel dependencies across scales and dimensions while disrupting semantic content. Reducing recognizable content is intended to reduce content bias in the features used for detection.

The resulting maps serve as input to a convolutional neural network classifier. In open-world experiments involving images from 32 generative models, the method substantially improves accuracy and generalization over state-of-the-art approaches. The finding supports entropy-based local patterns as useful detection features across diverse tested generators. It does not establish a universally source-invariant signature, but it provides empirical evidence that suppressing content cues while retaining statistical structure can improve generalization.
neurips-2025-mlep-multi-granularity-loca.tldr: MLEP uses multiscale entropy patterns from shuffled image patches to improve generated-image detection and generalization across 32 tested generators.

paragraphs: Automated machine learning systems can still require substantial expert configuration, especially when inputs span different modalities. MLZero uses multiple language-model agents to automate the workflow with minimal human intervention. Its first step is a cognitive perception module that converts raw multimodal inputs into context suitable for guiding the later stages.

The system then generates and revises code iteratively. Semantic and episodic memory support this process, targeting problems such as fabricated code and outdated knowledge of software interfaces. The architecture therefore combines understanding the input data with memory-assisted code generation, addressing two obstacles to taking an automated workflow from raw data through an ML solution.

On MLE-Bench Lite, MLZero leads the evaluated competitors in success rate and solution quality and earns six gold medals. On the authors' 25-task Multimodal AutoML Agent Benchmark, it reports a success rate of 0.92 and an average rank of 2.28. The authors also find that a version using an 8B language model outperforms full-size competing systems. These results support the effectiveness of the overall workflow across the tested modalities and tasks.
neurips-2025-mlzero-a-multi-agent-system.tldr: MLZero combines multimodal perception, multiple language-model agents, and memory-assisted coding to automate machine learning with strong benchmark results.

paragraphs: Working with tables involves more than answering questions about cells or translating natural language into SQL. Professional users also need models to understand, reason about, and manipulate tabular data. MMTU addresses the limited coverage of existing evaluations by assembling a broader benchmark of tasks drawn from research on tabular data.

The benchmark contains more than 28,000 questions across 25 real-world table tasks. Its focus is expert-level work associated with spreadsheets, databases, and computational notebooks. Solving these tasks requires a combination of table understanding, reasoning, and coding. This broader scope tests whether a model can bring several relevant capabilities together rather than succeed on a single familiar table task.

In the reported evaluation, GPT-5 scores around 69% and DeepSeek R1 around 57%. Those results show substantial room for improvement even among the evaluated frontier reasoning models. The benchmark's contribution is both a large evaluation resource and evidence that strong language or reasoning capabilities do not automatically translate into consistently strong performance across professional table workflows.
neurips-2025-mmtu-a-massive-multi-task-t.tldr: MMTU evaluates 25 professional table tasks with over 28,000 questions, revealing substantial gaps in the tested frontier models' capabilities.

paragraphs: Concept-based models make predictions through human-understandable concepts rather than relying solely on an opaque image representation. A typical approach extracts concept activations from an encoding of the whole image and applies a linear classifier. The paper argues that this global representation restricts expressiveness when a task depends on individual objects and more complex visual structure.

Object-Centric Concept Bottlenecks combine concept-based models with pretrained object-centric foundation models. The framework brings object-level representations into the concept bottleneck, aiming to improve predictive performance while retaining interpretable decisions. A key question is how to aggregate the concept encodings associated with objects so they can support a prediction about the visual input.

The authors evaluate the framework on complex image datasets and use ablations to study components including those aggregation strategies. OCB outperforms traditional concept-based models and supports interpretable decisions on complex visual tasks. The significance is that interpretable concepts need not be tied exclusively to a single holistic image encoding: organizing them around objects can make the approach more expressive in the evaluated settings.
neurips-2025-object-centric-concept-bott.tldr: Object-Centric Concept Bottlenecks combine object-level representations with interpretable concepts to improve performance on complex visual tasks.

paragraphs: Mixture-of-experts networks divide computation among expert networks through a gating mechanism. Their empirical efficiency is well established, but this paper asks what kinds of complex functions they can represent efficiently. The analysis focuses on two structural properties: low-dimensionality and sparsity. These properties are assumptions that make the approximation results possible.

For shallow networks, the authors prove efficient approximation of functions supported on low-dimensional manifolds. Although the surrounding input space may have many dimensions, the relevant function is confined to a lower-dimensional structure. Under this setting, the result shows how mixture-of-experts models can overcome the curse of dimensionality.

For deep networks, the authors show that a number of layers proportional to L, with E experts per layer, can approximate piecewise functions containing E to the power L pieces when compositional sparsity holds. This establishes an exponential number of structured pieces under the stated structure, rather than arbitrary exponential capability. The analysis also explains the roles of gates, expert networks, expert counts, and depth, providing theoretical guidance for architectural variants.
neurips-2025-on-the-expressive-power-of-.tldr: The paper proves efficient mixture-of-experts approximation results for functions with low-dimensional or compositionally sparse structure.

paragraphs: Modern Hopfield networks and transformer self-attention have a known connection: under an adiabatic approximation, the Hopfield update rule agrees with a self-attention layer. This paper investigates what happens beyond that approximation. It establishes a more general correspondence by adding a hidden-state variable derived from the Hopfield network to self-attention.

The resulting mechanism, modern Hopfield attention, allows attention scores to be inherited across transformer layers. This gives attention a form of continuity from the input toward the output. The authors study how those hidden states affect rank collapse and token uniformity, problems in deep transformers where representations lose diversity or become excessively similar.

Both theoretical analysis and empirical results show significant improvements to these problems. The authors also report systematic accuracy improvements when applying the mechanism to Vision Transformer or GPT, without adding trainable parameters. The contribution is therefore an architectural change motivated by associative memory that improves the tested models' attention behavior and accuracy. The findings demonstrate mitigation of representational collapse, rather than claiming that all deep-transformer difficulties are resolved.
neurips-2025-on-the-role-of-hidden-state.tldr: Modern Hopfield attention carries hidden attention states across layers, mitigating representation collapse and improving accuracy without adding trainable parameters.

paragraphs: Active statistical inference uses an AI model to help decide which labels to collect under a fixed labeling budget. It prioritizes observations where the model is uncertain, aiming to improve estimation accuracy. This strategy can backfire when uncertainty estimates are inaccurate: the resulting estimates may be noisier than those obtained by sampling uniformly.

The paper introduces robust sampling strategies that interpolate optimally between uniform and active sampling according to uncertainty-score quality. Ideas from robust optimization help control the risk of trusting misleading scores. The approach retains the opportunity to direct labels toward useful observations while accounting for the possibility that the model's uncertainty ranking is unreliable.

The stated guarantee is that the resulting estimator is never worse than the estimator based on uniform sampling. With reliable uncertainty estimates, it also usually outperforms standard active inference; that second claim is qualified rather than universal. Evaluations on real datasets from computational social science and survey research demonstrate practical utility. The contribution makes uncertainty-guided data collection more dependable by integrating a uniform-sampling safeguard into the allocation strategy.
neurips-2025-robust-sampling-for-active-.tldr: Robust sampling blends uniform and uncertainty-guided label collection, guaranteeing an estimator no worse than uniform sampling while exploiting reliable uncertainty scores.

paragraphs: Searching semi-structured records with natural language requires handling both exact constraints and approximate meaning. A query can refer to several fields and require implicit reasoning, while record schemas differ across domains. SSRB examines whether neural retrievers can directly index these collections and interpret such queries without a separate domain-customized formal querying solution.

The authors build a benchmark using language-model generation and filtering, together with language-model-based automatic evaluation. It includes 14 million objects covering 99 schemas in six domains, plus 8,485 test queries. The queries combine exact matching conditions with fuzzy semantic requirements, making the benchmark a test of whether retrieved records satisfy constraints as well as resemble the query in meaning.

Evaluation finds that current leading retrievers can achieve acceptable performance but still struggle to understand matching constraints precisely. Training dense retrievers within the target domain significantly improves performance. These findings identify both a useful direction and a remaining weakness: direct neural retrieval can handle heterogeneous records, but semantic relevance alone does not ensure accurate constraint satisfaction. SSRB provides a resource for studying that combination.
neurips-2025-ssrb-direct-natural-languag.tldr: SSRB benchmarks natural-language retrieval over 14 million semi-structured objects, revealing weaknesses in exact constraint understanding and benefits from in-domain training.

paragraphs: A visual world model predicts what an environment will look like as actions are taken. Diffusion-based world models can synthesize detailed images, but using only a few recent observations leaves them without lasting context. Generated scenes can then drift away from previously observed content, weakening consistency over an extended interaction.

StateSpaceDiffuser adds features from a state-space model that represents the full interaction history. The diffusion model uses these features to retain long-term context while preserving detailed image synthesis. The authors also introduce an evaluation protocol that asks whether a model can recreate previously seen content during long rollouts, directly testing the memory problem the architecture targets.

Experiments compare the method with a strong diffusion-only baseline in a two-dimensional navigation maze and a complex three-dimensional environment. StateSpaceDiffuser maintains coherent visual context for an order of magnitude more steps and produces consistent views in both settings. The finding supports combining persistent state representations with diffusion generation: visual quality and memory can be addressed together, rather than expecting recent observations alone to preserve an environment's history.
neurips-2025-statespacediffuser-bringing.tldr: StateSpaceDiffuser adds state-space memory to diffusion world models, maintaining coherent visual context for an order of magnitude more steps than a strong baseline.

paragraphs: This paper studies tactile perception by training temporal neural networks on realistic input sequences from a customized rodent whisker-array simulator. An Encoder-Attender-Decoder framework provides a common setting for comparing architectures. The goal is both to improve artificial tactile categorization and to identify representations that align with activity in rodent somatosensory cortex.

Convolutional recurrent networks outperform purely feedforward and state-space encoders on tactile categorization. Their representations closely match the neural data, saturating explainable neural variability in the reported evaluation. The authors also find a clear linear relationship between supervised categorization performance and neural alignment, connecting task success with the quality of the neural fit.

A contrastive self-supervised version, trained with tactile-specific augmentations, matches the supervised models' neural fits without requiring category labels. This provides a label-free proxy that the authors regard as relevant to animal learning. Together, the findings highlight nonlinear recurrence as important for the tactile representations studied and support recurrent architectures with tailored self-supervision for artificial tactile perception. Neural alignment is the reported evidence, rather than proof that the models reproduce every aspect of biological processing.
neurips-2025-task-optimized-convolutiona.tldr: Convolutional recurrent tactile models excel at categorization and closely align with rodent neural activity, with self-supervised training matching supervised neural fits.

paragraphs: As visual language models become better at reasoning across images, their reasoning capabilities can interact with safety objectives in problematic ways. This paper investigates that tension through Visualization-of-Thought Attack, or VoTA. The framework tests whether models maintain safety when asked to process chains of images containing risky visual reasoning.

VoTA automatically constructs these image chains to challenge a victim model's safety behavior. The authors describe the attack as exploiting a conflict between following the visual reasoning and enforcing safety protocols. Its contribution is an evaluation of vulnerability associated with multimodal reasoning sequences, rather than considering image understanding and safety as independent capabilities.

Across nine open-source and six commercial visual language models, the reported average attack success rate increases from 63.70% to 90.41% compared with state-of-the-art methods. That is a difference of 26.71 percentage points. The results show a substantial weakness in the evaluated systems when processing these insecure visual thought sequences. They motivate stronger safety alignment for multimodal reasoning, while remaining evidence about the tested attacks and models rather than every possible visual interaction.
neurips-2025-towards-visualization-of-th.tldr: VoTA exposes safety weaknesses in visual reasoning, raising average attack success from 63.70% to 90.41% across 15 evaluated visual language models.

paragraphs: When scene text is visually ambiguous or lacks familiar meaning, a multimodal model may produce a plausible phrase that does not match the image. The paper calls this semantic hallucination. Its investigation finds that transformer layers attending more strongly to scene-text regions are less prone to these errors, suggesting an internal signal for improving decoding.

The proposed training-free framework combines two components. ZoomText locates potential text regions through a coarse-to-fine process without an external detector. Grounded Layer Correction adaptively uses representations from layers less prone to hallucination to guide output generation. The aim is to correct visually unsupported answers for non-semantic text while preserving the meaning of meaningful text.

The authors also introduce TextHalu-Bench, containing 1,740 semantic and non-semantic samples with manually curated question–answer pairs. Experiments show reduced semantic hallucination and strong results on public scene-text spotting and understanding benchmarks. The contribution links a measured relationship inside the model to a decoding intervention, using visual grounding already present in selected layers to reduce the tendency to replace uncertain text with a plausible interpretation.
neurips-2025-when-semantics-mislead-visi.tldr: A training-free framework locates scene text and guides decoding with better-grounded internal layers to reduce semantically plausible but visually incorrect answers.
